chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Qays said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Most of those who come to me from among my brothers, I have set a limit for me in dealing with them that I do not allow to others.' He said: 'If you entrust your brother [with your goods], that is good; but if not, sell [your goods] with the sale of the discerning one.'

key_terms.بَيْعَ الْبَصِيرِ الْمُدَاقِّ: the sale of the discerning/insightful one

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on trading with friends or relatives?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) advises a merchant on how to handle trade with his friends or brothers. If the merchant trusts his friend to sell his goods, he may entrust him; otherwise, he should sell his own goods personally with the care and discernment of an expert, implying that entrusting friends can lead to disputes or loss if not managed with clear limits.
